preview.name: strip-ansi-cli
preview.description:
Need terminal text without ANSI escape codes? strip-ansi-cli provides a command-line filter for that job.

Pipe a colored directory listing into strip-ansi to remove its escape codes.

The usage also accepts text directly as an argument, or piped from another command.

The tests supply ANSI-styled foo followed by foo, and expect foofoo through both interfaces.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body:
Inside cli.js, input means the first positional argument. If it is falsy and stdin is a TTY, execution stops with Input required and status one.

A truthy first argument goes to init. Only with falsy input and non-TTY stdin does the program await getStdin instead.

Both processing routes share init, which delegates stripping to the imported strip-ansi function.

It writes the transformed string directly to standard output, adding no newline of its own.
